name: Nicanor
overview: Nicanor was a male figure in the early Christian community who was chosen to serve the widows of the Hellenistic Jews. Scripture does not specify his tribe or provide additional personal notes. His role highlights the practical care and organization within the early church.
namesAndTitles: The name Nicanor appears without a given meaning or divine origin in the biblical text. It is presented simply as a proper name without further explanation in the Scripture reference provided.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Nicanor beyond his service role among the Hellenistic Jewish widows. There are no listed familial connections or titles beyond his appointed ministry.
scriptureSignificance: Nicanor's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his appointment as one of the seven chosen to address the needs of widows among the Hellenistic Jewish believers. This appointment reflects the early church's commitment to organized ministry and care within the body of Christ, ensuring that practical needs were met alongside the preaching of the Word.
